description: A class-level rule reads its own instance's properties with leading dots
code:
class Line(qty, price):
    this.qty = qty
    this.price = price
$Line.total = .qty * .price
first = Line(2, 3)
second = Line(4, 5)
assert([first.total, second.total], [6, 20])
first.price = 10
[first.total, second.total]

description: A nested receiver reads the properties of the target's own object
code:
shop = {owner: {first: "Ada", last: "Byron"}}
shop.owner.name = .first + " " + .last
assert(shop.owner.name, "Ada Byron")
shop.owner.last = "King"
shop.owner.name

description: A constructor reads this through leading dots and stays live
code:
class Rect(w, h):
    this.w = w
    this.h = h
    this.area = .w * .h
r = Rect(3, 4)
assert(r.area, 12)
r.h = 5
r.area

description: Compound and value assignments read the receiver of their target
code:
meter = {reading: 10, step: 2}
meter.reading += .step
assert(meter.reading, 12)
meter.snapshot := .reading
meter.step = 5
[meter.reading, meter.snapshot]

description: A Python-style conditional and a template read the receiver
code:
item = {name: "lamp", stock: 0}
item.status = "open" if .stock > 0 else "sold"
item.label = `${.name}: ${.status}`
assert(item.label, "lamp: sold")
item.stock = 3
item.label

description: A lambda inside a class-level rule compares every instance with the computed one
code:
class Cell(h):
    this.h = h
$Cell.rank = Cell.filter(other -> other.h > .h).length + 1
low = Cell(1)
high = Cell(5)
mid = Cell(3)
assert([low.rank, high.rank, mid.rank], [3, 1, 2])
low.h = 9
[low.rank, high.rank, mid.rank]

description: A call argument that starts with a dot stays a selector beside receiver reads
Rollback restores a property rule that reads its receiver
code:
account = {balance: 5, rate: 2}
account.interest = .balance * .rate
try:
    account.rate = 10
    assert(account.interest, 50)
    throw "UNDO"
catch error:
    assert(error, "UNDO")
[account.rate, account.interest]
